entries.note: Object pronoun rendered les coupables; idiom burning anger translated as colère ardente.
Following construction merged; Hebrew two occurrences of קבה are distinct (tent and lower abdomen).
Zeal and jealousy translated zèle and colère respectively.
Name construction recast as s’appelait; repeated striking participles condensed.
Explicit independent pronoun refers to Tsur and is implicit in French.
Relative expansion qui eut lieu requires review. Native 25:19 belongs to LSG 26:1 and is not included.
Negative possessive construction recast as n’avait point de fils.
Possessive suffix on cause is implicit in French.
Emphatic infinitive and repeated inheritance expressions retained.
French negative sanctification reflects the context of rebellion, not an explicit Hebrew negative in this clause.
Causative going out and coming in distinguished from intransitive verbs.
Possession and imparting dignity restructured; contextual pronominal links.
Both speech-authority phrases refer to Eleazar; French explicitly names Joshua and Eleazar where Hebrew uses pronouns.
